sections.content: Looking at the current image, after clicking on the red block, the character's body is now orange (O) and the green frame is gone (or changed). Let me check the color counts.

sections.label: TOOL CALL: python
sections.content:
<tool_call>
<function=python>
<parameter=code>
# Check current color counts
seg = current_frame.segmentation['nodes']
current_colors = {}
for n in seg:
    c = n['color']
    current_colors[c] = current_colors.get(c, 0) + n['pixels']
print("Current color counts:", current_colors)

# Check what changed from previous frame
if previous_frame:
    prev_seg = previous_frame.segmentation['nodes']
    prev_colors = {}
    for n in prev_seg:
        c = n['color']
        prev_colors[c] = prev_colors.get(c, 0) + n['pixels']
    print("\nPrevious color counts:", prev_colors)
    print("Changes:")
    all_colors = set(list(current_colors.keys()) + list(prev_colors.keys()))
    for c in all_colors:
        diff = current_colors.get(c, 0) - prev_colors.get(c, 0)
        if diff != 0:
            print(f"  {c}: {prev_colors.get(c, 0)} -> {current_colors.get(c, 0)} (diff={diff})")

# Let me also check all unique colors in the entire history to understand the game
print("\nAll colors seen in history:")
all_colors_seen = set()
for h in history:
    seg_h = h.frame.segmentation['nodes']
    for n in seg_h:
        all_colors_seen.add(n['color'])
print(sorted(all_colors_seen))
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>

sections.content:
<tool_call>
<function=python>
<parameter=code>

for i, h in enumerate(history):
    seg_h = h.frame.segmentation['nodes']
    colors_h = {}
    for n in seg_h:
        c = n['color']
        colors_h[c] = colors_h.get(c, 0) + n['pixels']
    if 'G' in colors_h:
        print(f"Step {i}: action={h.action}, G={colors_h['G']}, colors={colors_h}")

# Now let me try clicking on the orange pixels to see what happens
seg = current_frame.segmentation['nodes']

# Try clicking on the first orange node
if orange_nodes:
    on = orange_nodes[0]
    boundary = on['boundary']
    rows = [p[0] for p in boundary]
    cols = [p[1] for p in boundary]
    center_row = sum(rows) // len(rows)
    center_col = sum(cols) // len(cols)
    print(f"Clicking on orange at row={center_row}, col={center_col}")
    action([{'action': 'MOUSE', 'row': center_row, 'col': center_col}])
